rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The better reading takes ṣalāt as care and the display of honor, a shared sense underlying mercy, prayer, and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: والأحسن خلافه وأن الصلاة للاعتناء وإظهار الشرف كما قاله الغزالي وغيره وهو قدر مشترك بين الرحمة والدعاء والاستغفار

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats “those who believe in what was sent to you” as a coordinated description of the same people named before.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري في قوله تعالى ﴿ والذين يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that coordination of descriptions requires different meanings, whereas what was sent to the Prophet is the very unseen already mentioned.
rows.anchor: واعترض عليه بأن شرط عطف الصفة على الصفة تغاير الصفتين في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible defense is that the second description specifies a particular part of the general unseen, making this coordination of particular after general.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقال المعطوف عليه مطلق الغيب والمعطوف غيب خاص فيكون من عطف الخاص على العام

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some commentators take “the illuminating Book” to mean the Psalms and treat the coordinated nouns as descriptions of one thing.
rows.anchor: وجعل منه بعضهم قوله تعالى ﴿ وإن يكذبوك فقد كذب الذين من قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that reading: repeating the preposition after the conjunction signals strong separation and avoids coordinating a thing with itself.
rows.anchor: وهذا يرده تكرار الباء فانه يشعر بالفصل لآن فائدة تكرار العامل بعد حرف العطف إشعار بقوة الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers a fresh meaning: “they came to them” includes the Prophet among the messengers, and the illuminating Book is the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أنه للتأسيس وبيانه وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then He seized those who disbelieved” connects to their earlier denial; placing the proof before that clause is an emphatic parenthesis highlighting the establishment of the evidence.
rows.anchor: وجاء تقديم قيام الحجة عليهم قبل العطف اعتراضا للاهتمام به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from direct address to third-person narration includes the Prophet in the report and conveys wonder, broadening the account to all hearers; the author compares two other verses.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ جاؤوا ﴾ انصراف من الخطاب إلى الغيبة كأنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ opens with Moses’s beginnings, support, and refusal to aid wrongdoers, then closes by paralleling the Prophet’s departure from Mecca and promise of return.
rows.anchor: وختمها بأمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بألا يكون ظهيرا للكافرين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī highlights the contrast between al-Muʾminūn’s opening, “the believers have succeeded,” and its ending, “the disbelievers do not succeed.”
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشرى وقد جعل الله فاتحة سورة المؤمنين ﴿ قد أفلح المؤمنون ﴾ وأورد فى خاتمتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qad may precede a perfect verb or an imperfect verb, provided the imperfect has no jussive, subjunctive, or future particle before it.
rows.anchor: تدخل على الماضي المتصرف وعلى المضارع بشرط تجرده عن الجازم والناصب وحرف التنفيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle qad has five uses: expectation, approximation, diminution, abundance, and confirmation.
rows.anchor: وتأتي لخمس معان التوقع والتقريب والتقليل والتكثير والتحقيق

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl explains qad in “prayer has been established” as addressing a congregation waiting for the prayer to begin; likewise, “he has sat” can announce awaited good.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل إن قولك قد قعد كلام لقول ينتظرون الخير ومنه قول المؤذن قد قامت الصلاة لأن الجماعة منتظرون

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik’s wording suggests that qad with a perfect verb brings the event near to the present rather than marking expectation; al-Zarkashī allows both senses.
rows.anchor: وظاهر كلام ابن مالك في تسهيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a perfect verb, expectation can mean that the event was anticipated and has now occurred; qad therefore suits matters awaited by the hearers.
rows.anchor: ولكن معنى التوقع فيه إن قد تدل على أنه كان متوقعا منتظرا ثم صار ماضيا ولذلك تستعمل في الأشياء المترقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with qad is appropriate when answering an expectation: the audience awaited knowledge of its standing before God, and the woman awaited an answer to her prayer.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه ليس من الوجه الابتداء بها إلا أن تكون جوابا لمتوقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a perfect verb, qad marks approximation to the present and is required when that verb occurs as a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وأما التقريب فإنها ترد للدلالة عليه مع الماضي فقد فتدخل لتقريبه من الحال ولذلك تلزم قد مع الماضي إذا وقع حالا

rows.speaker: المبرد والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Farrāʾ posit an implicit qad before “our goods have been returned to us”; others reject supplying an omitted particle.
rows.anchor: هذا مذهب المبرد والفراء وغيرهما

rows.speaker: ابن عصفور
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṣfūr says an affirmative perfect in an oath answer takes qad and the lām when near the present, but only the lām when remote.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عصفور إن جواب القسم بالماضي المتصرف المثبت إن كان قريبا من زمن الحال دخلت عليه قد واللام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s discussion of “We sent Noah” in an oath answer reads qad with the perfect as signaling expectation.
rows.anchor: وكلام الزمخشري يدل على أن قد مع الماضي في جواب القسم للتوقع

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī considers “God permitted trade” ambiguous because usury is ambiguous and functions like an unknown exception from trade.
rows.anchor: وللشافعي رحمه الله قول بإجمال البيع لأن الربا مجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects ambiguity: usury broadly covers increases, and excluding some cases is specification that does not alter the word’s lexical force.
rows.anchor: والصحيح الأول فإن الربا عام في الزيادات كلها وكون البعض غير مراد نوع تخصيص فلا تتغير به دلالة الأوضاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From dawn” clarifies the previously ambiguous distinction between the white and black threads: the intended contrast is day and night.
rows.anchor: ومثال النوع الثاني قوله تعالى ﴿ من الفجر ﴾ فإنه فسر مجمل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعض الصحابة
rows.claim: Some Companions reportedly tied white and black threads to a foot and kept eating until their colors could be distinguished, after which “from dawn” clarified the meaning.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد أن بعض الصحابة كان يربط في رجله الخيط الأبيض والأسود ولا يزال يأكل ويشرب حتى يتبين له لونهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later ruling that a divorced woman is not lawful until she marries another clarifies that “divorce is twice” means revocable divorce, although the clarification is in another verse.
rows.anchor: فإنه دل على أن المراد بقوله تعالى ﴿ الطلاق مرتان ﴾ الطلاق الرجعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces looking toward their Lord establish the permissibility of seeing God and interpret “sights do not perceive Him” as denying encompassing vision, not vision itself.
rows.anchor: ومثال الثاني قوله تعالى ﴿ وجوه يومئذ ناضرة إلى ربها ناظرة ﴾ فإنه دل على جواز الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wicked being veiled from their Lord in humiliation implies that the righteous will see Him, resolving the ambiguity of “sights do not perceive Him.”
rows.anchor: وأيضا قوله تعالى ﴿ كلا إنهم عن ربهم يومئذ لمحجوبون ﴾ فإنه لما حجب الفجار عن رؤيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One kind of omitted object is still intended and recovered from context; a verb or relative clause can require it, so the deletion is understood as ellipsis for brevity.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون مقصودا مع الحذف فينوى لدليل ويقدر في كل موضع ما يليق به

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the phrase without the final object pronoun; on that reading “what their hands made” is coordinated with “its fruit.”
rows.anchor: في قراءة حمزة والكسائي بغير هاء أي ما عملته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mā can be negative: people eat the fruit though their hands did not make it, a stronger expression of blessing supported by the reminder that God makes crops grow.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ما نافية والمعنى ليأكلوا من ثمره ولم تعمله أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects treating “he drinks from what you drink” as object deletion, since the verb drink can take an object directly.
rows.anchor: وهو فاسد لأن شرب يتعدى بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omission can shorten speech when context supplies the object: “show me” means “show me Yourself”; the author offers reverence or longing as possible reasons for the wording.
rows.anchor: منها قصد الاختصار عند قيام القرائن والقرائن إما حالية كما في قوله تعالى ﴿ رب أرني أنظر إليك ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Moses’s prospective employer’s condition, “that you hire me” omits the object “yourself.”
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه متعد حذف مفعوله أي تأجرني نفسك

rows.speaker: السكاكي
rows.claim: Al-Sakkākī counts five omitted objects in the account of Moses at Midian, on the reading with kasra on the dāl in yuṣdir.
rows.anchor: وجعل منه السكاكي قوله تعالى ﴿ ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author judges those five cases more likely to belong to the second category of object omission.
rows.anchor: والأقرب أنه من الضرب الثاني كما سنبينه فيه إن شاء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that God may show mercy is linked to the Banū Naḍīr, whom the Prophet besieged, captured, killed, and expelled.
rows.anchor: وهذه في بني النضير وقد سباهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقتلهم وأبادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage reads the two conditional promises as unrealized conditions: if the wives were divorced God would replace them, and if the people returned He would show mercy; they did not do these things, so “perhaps” retains its ordinary sense.
rows.anchor: وهذا عندي متأول لأن الأول تقديره إن طلقكن يبدله وما فعل فهذا شرط يقع فيه الجزاء ولم يفعله والثاني تقديره إن عدتم رحمكم وهم أصروا وعسى على بابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage gives two analyses of ʿasā’s tense: past in wording and meaning because hope arose in the present, or past in wording but future in meaning because the reported hope is to occur.
rows.anchor: قال وعسى ماضي اللفظ والمعنى لأنه طمع وذلك حصل في شيء مستقبل وقال قوم ماضي اللفظ مستقبل في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the first construction, ʿasā takes an explicit subject and a verbal infinitive as its complement; it does not take a participial complement, which does not mark past time.
rows.anchor: أحدهما ترفع اسما صريحا ويؤتى بعده بخبر ويلزم كونه فعلا مضارعا نحو عسى زيد أن يقوم فلا يجوز قائما

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans parse the infinitive after ʿasā as nominative in apposition, but the author objects that it cannot be omitted and can be advanced.
rows.anchor: وقال الكوفيون في موضع رفع بدل ورد بأنه لا يجوز تركه ويجوز تقديمه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the second construction, the infinitive itself is ʿasā’s subject, as in “perhaps he will rise”; it then needs no accusative complement.
rows.anchor: الثاني أن يكون المرفوع بها أن والفعل وهو عسى أن يقوم زيد فلا يفتقر هنا إلى منصوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “perhaps your Lord will raise you,” rabbuka cannot be the subject of ʿasā because that would split the relative clause; in “perhaps you dislike,” the pronouns belong to the verbs, not ʿasā.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز رفع ربك ب عسى لئلا يلزم الفصل بين الصلة والموصول بالأجنبي

rows.speaker: عبد القاهر
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Qāhir says that when a question is spoken, an answer usually omits the verb and gives only a noun; an unspoken question needs an explicit verb because its cue is weak.
rows.anchor: وذكر الشيخ عبد القاهر إن السؤال إذا كان ملفوظا به فالأكثر ترك الفعل في الجواب والاقتصار على الاسم وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The open-bāʾ reading of “men glorify Him” challenges that rule: it supplies the verb as the answer to an implicit “who glorifies Him?” question.
rows.anchor: فيمن قراها بفتح الباء كأنه قيل من يسبحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says an explicit question is best answered with a verb and explains other Qur’anic “he said” clauses as answering omitted questions, such as the visitors’ greeting and Pharaoh’s question about God.
rows.anchor: نعم الأولى ذكر الفعل لما ذكر وعليه يخرج كل ما ورد في القران من لفظ قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning both the prohibition on saying “uff” and on rebuking parents emphasizes the first ban as if it were prohibited twice, implicitly and explicitly.
rows.anchor: وإنما عدل عن ذلك للاهتمام بالنهي عن التأفيف والعناية بالنهي حتى كأنه قال نهى عنه مرتين مرة بالمفهوم وأخرى بالمنطوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sina is drowsiness before sleep, while sleep is a heavier swoon that affects the heart; mentioning both denies the mistaken thought that only the weaker state is excluded.
rows.anchor: فإن النوم غشية ثقيلة تقع على القلب تمنعه معرفة الأشياء والسنة مما يتقدمه من النعاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God reinforces that sleep and any sharing in His authority are impossible, since He created them and their contents.
rows.anchor: لأنه خلقهما بما فيهما والمشاركة إنما تقع فيما فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “does not seize Him” means sleep cannot overpower Him; the added negation before sleep excludes both drowsiness and sleep in every state.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فإنه يلزم من نفي النسة نفي النوم أنه لم يقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praiseful descriptions should progress from lesser to greater, since reversing the order makes the lesser redundant; rhetoricians give three views on whether “virtuous” or “perfect” is stronger, including that they are equal.
rows.anchor: وإذا ذكرت صفات فإن كانت للمدح فالأولى الانتقال فيها من الأدنى إلى الأعلى ليكون المدح متزايدا بتزايد الكلام

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الشيباني
rows.claim: One lexical meaning of āya is a group: Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī cites the expression “the people went out with their āya,” meaning their group.
rows.anchor: أحدها جماعة الحروف قال أبو عمرو الشيباني تقول العرب خرج القوم بآيتهم أي بجماعتهم

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: Āya can also mean a marvel; the cited poet calls someone a wonder in beauty with no equal.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر … آية فى الجمال ليس له فى ال … حسن شبه وما له من نظير

rows.speaker: العرب
rows.claim: Āya can mean a sign or trace, as in saying that no sign remained in a ruined house; each Qur’anic verse is a sign of Muhammad’s prophethood.
rows.anchor: ثالثها العلامة تقول العرب خربت دار فلان وما بقى فيها آية أي علامة فكأن كل آية في القرآن علامة ودلالة على نبوة محمد

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh derives āya from ayya, on the faʿla pattern: the yāʾ moves and the preceding vowel opens to produce āya.
rows.anchor: فقال سيبويه فعلة بفتح العين وأصلها أيية

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī derives āya from āyiyah and says the first yāʾ was deleted to avoid the gemination seen in dābbah.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي أصلها آيية على وزن فاعلة حذفت الياء الأولى مخافة أن يلتزم فيها من الإدغام ما لزم في دابة

rows.speaker: الجعبرى
rows.claim: Al-Jaʿbarī defines an āya technically as a Qur’anic unit made of clauses, actually or by estimation, with a beginning and end within a sūra; the name derives from sign or group.
rows.anchor: فقال الجعبرى فى كتاب المفرد فى معرفة العدد حد الآية قرآن مركب

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another definition is a portion of Qur’an separated from what precedes and follows it, with no counterpart elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره الآية طائفة من القرآن منقطعة عما قبلها وما بعدها ليس بينها شبه بما سواها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view defines an āya as one of the counted units in a sūra, named for proving the messenger’s truth and challengers’ inability.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي الواحدة من المعدودات في السور سميت به لأنها علامة على صدق من أتى بها وعلى عجز المتحدي بها

rows.speaker: الواحدي وبعض أصحابنا
rows.claim: A further view says an āya marks the interruption of one passage from another; al-Wāḥidī and colleagues note that this could imply calling a shorter unit an āya, were its present limits not fixed by transmission.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدى وبعض أصحابنا يجوز على هذا القول تسمية أقل من الآية آية لولا أن التوقيف ورد بما هي عليه الآن

rows.speaker: ابن المنير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munīr says that “dark green” is the Qur’an’s only one-word āya.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المنير فى البحر ليس فى القرآن كلمة واحدة آية إلا ﴿ مدهامتان ﴾

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some hold that verse boundaries, like sūra boundaries, are known only through prophetic instruction, defining an āya as a transmitted group of letters set apart in meaning from its surroundings.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم الصحيح أنها إنما تعلم بتوقيف من الشارع لا مجال للقياس فيه كمعرفة السورة فالآية طائفة حروف من القرآن علم بالتوقيف انقطاعها معنى

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الشهرابانى
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Shahrabānī says Abū Bakr al-Naysābūrī first made the study of textual correspondence prominent in Baghdad, asking why verses and sūras are placed beside one another.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ أبو الحسن الشهرابانى أول من أظهر ببغداد علم المناسبة ولم نكن سمعناه من غيره هو الشيخ الإمام أبو بكر النيسابورى

rows.speaker: عز الدين بن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salām says correspondence is useful when a discourse has one connected subject, but insisting on links among revelations with different causes and rulings is strained.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ عز الدين بن عبد السلام المناسبة علم حسن ولكن يشترط في حسن ارتباط الكلام أن يقع في أمر متحد مرتبط أوله بآخره

rows.speaker: بعض مشايخنا المحققين
rows.claim: Some exacting scholars answer that revelation followed events while the muṣḥaf order follows wisdom and prophetic instruction, matching the heavenly archetype; its arrangement is part of its manifest inimitability.
rows.anchor: قال بعض مشايخنا المحققين قد وهم من قال لا يطلب للآي الكريمة مناسبة لأنها حسب الوقائع المتفرقة وفصل الخطاب أنها على حسب الوقائع تنزيلا وعلى حسب الحكمة ترتيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The method is first to decide whether a verse completes the preceding one or stands independently; if independent, ask how it relates to what came before, and apply the same inquiry to sūras.
rows.anchor: والذي ينبغي في كل آية أن يبحث أول كل شيء عن كونها مكملة لما قبلها أو مستقلة ثم المستقلة ما وجه مناسبتها لما قبلها

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the disagreement over an omitted circumstantial element is about analogy: Sībawayh restricts it to attested usage, while al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad analogize it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي لا خلاف بين سيبويه وأبي العباس في الحال المحذوف الذي المصدر منصوب به وإنما الخلاف بينهما في القياس

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: On al-Kisāʾī’s lightened reading, the phrase is an alert plus a vocative—“O these, prostrate”—or two alerts without a vocative, combined to draw the commanded person’s attention.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ ألا يسجدوا ﴾ 1 على قراءة الكسائي بتخفيف ألا على أنها تنبيه ويا نداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the majority’s strengthened reading, أن governs the imperfect and لا negates it; the verb is inflected and loses its nūn as the sign of the subjunctive.
rows.anchor: وأما على قراءة الأكثر بالتشديد فعلى أن أن الناصبة للفعل دخلت عليها لا النافية والفعل المضارع بعدها منصوب وحذفت النون علامة النصب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One light reading of “or one who is devout” treats the hamza as a vocative: “O possessor of these qualities.”
rows.anchor: وقد قيل في قوله تعالى ﴿ أم من هو قانت آناء الليل ﴾ 4 في قراءة تخفيف من إن الهمزة فيه للنداء

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Fāris says the particle alā may express regret and grief, as in “will they not prostrate”; another view takes it as an alert particle.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس تأنى للتأسف والتلهف نحو ﴿ ألا يسجدوا ﴾ 5 وقيل للتنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alā can also express delight, as in the cited line wishing that the beloved’s coolness on the heart would stay.
rows.anchor: وللتلذذ نحو … يا بردها على الفؤاد لو تقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object pronoun in “if the All-Merciful wills” signifies that the servant cannot know God’s will directly, but assents to it through demonstrative faith.
rows.anchor: وكذلك ضمير العبد مثل ﴿ إن يردن الرحمن ﴾ غائب عن علم إرادته الرحمن إنما علمه بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified “people” in “fear them not, but fear Me” is universal and unknown in its reality, so God alone is the proper object of complete fear; the other verse concerns particular wrongdoers who appeared openly.
rows.anchor: الناس كلي لا يدل على ناس بأعيانهم ولا موصوفين بصفة فهم كلي ولا يعلم الكلي من حيث هو كلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting the yāʾ in “announce glad tidings to My servants” and “say, My servants” reflects that the Prophet alone directly receives the address, while the servants learn it through him.
rows.anchor: وكذلك حذفت الياء من ﴿ فبشر عباد ﴾ و ﴿ قل يا عباد ﴾ فإنه خطاب لرسوله عليه السلام على الخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ and vocative remain in “My servants, no fear is upon you” because the people of the afterlife hear the direct address without a veil.
rows.anchor: فإنها ثبتت لأنه خطاب لهم فى الاخرة غير محجوبين عنه

words: قُلْ يَٰعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preserved yāʾ and vocative in the call to servants who exceeded the bounds summon them from Islam and obedience toward the station of spiritual excellence; the author gives a similar reading for believers in al-ʿAnkabūt.
rows.anchor: وكذلك ﴿ يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على ﴾ ثبت الضمير وحرف النداء فى الخط فإنه دعاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In supplication, the yāʾ and vocative may both be omitted: people cannot comprehend God, while He is nearer to them than themselves.
rows.anchor: وكذلك سقطتا فى موطن الدعاء مثل ﴿ رب اغفر لي ﴾ حذفت الياء لعدم الإحاطة به عند التوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “his saying, ‘My Lord,’” the vocative remains because the speaker calls God while present among the people, while the possessive self-reference is dropped in the inward station of self-effacement.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله ﴿ وقيله يا رب ﴾ فأثبت حرف النداء لأنه دعا ربه من مرتبة حضوره معهم فى مقام الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An interrogative with an imperfect can deny that an act occurs at all, as in “shall we force it upon you?”; it can also warn someone against taking a dangerous course.
rows.anchor: وفيه دخول الاستفهام على المضارع فإذا قلت أتفعل أو أأنت تفعل احتمل وجهين أحدهما إنكار وجود الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the object redirects the censure to whether the agent is fit to perform the act, as in “shall I take a patron other than God?”
rows.anchor: والثاني قولك لمن يركب الخطر أتذهب في غير طريق انظر لنفسك واستبصر فإذا قدمت المفعول توجه الإنكار إلى كونه بمثابة أن يوقع به مثل ذلك الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rejecting question can insinuate that the addressee claimed or committed the rejected thing, accusing them of a false assertion explicitly or by implication.
rows.anchor: الثاني قد يصحب الإنكار التكذيب للتعريض بأن المخاطب ادعاه وقصد تكذيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes invalidating rejection, where the claimed act is unreal and its claimant false, from genuine rebuke, where the act occurred but its agent is blameworthy.
rows.anchor: والحاصل ان الانكار قسمان ابطالي وحقيقي فالابطالي ان يكون ما بعدها غير واقع ومدعيه كاذب
